neighbours.label: A word piece inside a variant spelling or root gloss that partly repeats a name just given, usually in brackets (Gaulden (Gaul⟦ding⟧, …), Qing (Ch'⟦ing⟧), Acanthocephala (acanth⟦o⟧ = spiny))
fire: Records of the Thornbury (Thornberry, Thornbery) family go back to 1640.
The capital was then called Peking (Pei-ching) in most Western atlases.
The genus Triceratops takes its name from Greek (tri = three, cerat = horn, ops = face).
The poet Li Bai (Li Po, Li Bo) wrote during the Tang period.
Her ancestors appear in the parish register as Whitcombe (Whitcomb, Witcombe).
Biologists coined Hippopotamus from two roots (hippo = horse, potamus = river).
The philosopher Laozi (Lao-tzu, Lao-tse) is credited with the short classic.
The village of Kirkby (Kirby, Kirkeby) is listed in the old survey.
quiet: Records of the Thornbury family go back to 1640 and fill three boxes.
The capital was then a walled city (rebuilt twice) in most Western accounts.
The genus Triceratops lived late in the Cretaceous (about 68 million years ago).
The poet Li Bai (who died in 762) wrote during the Tang period.
Her ancestors appear in the parish register as farmers (and later as millers).
Biologists first described the animal from two specimens (a skull and a hide).
The philosopher (if he existed at all) is credited with the short classic.
The village of Kirkby (population 900) is listed in the old survey.

notes: Card: no single token; peaks sit on the piece where a bracketed variant or etymological root departs from the name before it. Probes: Qing (Ch'ing) 0.55, Greek-root gloss 0.46, surname variants 0.38; a bracketed acronym 0.04, no gloss 0.01-0.04.
